title: Mistaking Shadows for Reality
paragraphs: In Book Seven of the Republic, Plato asks his readers to imagine prisoners who have spent their whole lives chained inside a cave. They face a blank wall and cannot turn their heads. Behind them, a fire burns, and figures carried in front of it cast moving shadows on the wall. Since the prisoners have never seen anything else, they take the shadows to be reality.

Plato then imagines one prisoner being freed and forced to walk towards the light. The glare is painful, and at first the man wants to return to the familiar shadows. Gradually, however, his eyes adjust, and he comes to see trees, rivers and finally the sun itself. Plato suggests that this is how the mind moves from opinion to understanding.

The freed man goes back to tell the others, but his eyes now struggle in the dark. The prisoners conclude that the journey has damaged him, and they refuse to leave. Readers have long seen the story as a comment on education: real learning can be uncomfortable, and those who gain new insight may not be welcomed by the people they left behind.

options.text: A guide to ancient Greek theatre

options.explanation: Metin mağara alegorisini ve öğrenmeyle ilişkisini anlatır.

questions.prompt: What do the prisoners believe the shadows are?

options.text: They believe the shadows are dangerous spirits.
They believe the shadows are real.
They believe the shadows are a game.
They believe the shadows come from the sun.

questions.prompt: What does “adjust” mean in the second paragraph?

options.explanation: Ateş geçer ama kelime bunu demez.
Adjust, yeni duruma alışmak, uyum sağlamak demektir.

questions.prompt: Why do the prisoners refuse to leave?

options.text: They think the journey harmed him
options.explanation: Mahkûmlar yolculuğun ona zarar verdiği sonucuna varır.

options.text: They are afraid of the fire behind them
They think he has become wiser than them
options.explanation: Metin onların adamın zarar gördüğünü düşündüğünü söyler.

options.text: They were told to stay by the guards

sources.claim: Platon'un Devlet'inde (Kitap VII, 514a-520a) mağara alegorisi: ömür boyu zincirli mahkûmlar ateşin duvara düşürdüğü gölgeleri gerçek sanır; serbest kalan biri ışığa çıkar, gözleri alışır, sonra dönüp anlattığında diğerleri ona inanmaz.
